newsitem.title: INDIA: India forms group for infrastructure investment.
newsitem.headline: India forms group for infrastructure investment.

text.p: India plans to set up an inter-institutional group consisting of leading financial institutions and state-owned banks to draw investment into infrastructure, a Finance Ministry statement said on Tuesday.
The statement said the group would have four panels, including one for power, telecommunications, ports and roads.

"The sub-groups will interact with private investors and make special recommendations to resolve problems in infrastructure areas. Based on their recommendations, the Finance Ministry will take action," it said.

India needs investment worth $30 billion for roads over the next five years. In telecommunications, total investment committed in licence fees to the government over the next 15 years is about $22 billion.
Investment between $15 billion and $20 billion is required to upgrade existing port infrastructure, according to the Surface Transport Ministry.
And in power, India needs $80 billion by 2002 to meet current demand projections, according to the Power Ministry.
